local_lite.last_unpaced_video: Five NV12 frames matched, four Present calls returned and the next Present began before the reboot.

external_oled.graphics: The author integrated mesa-switch-woa WDDM and tgd3d/NVK on Mariko OLED.
external_oled.platform: Windows inbox sdbus behind an EL2 SDMMC trap, SwitchWifi from the shared driver project, and a separate swbatt GPU power bridge. The Lite platform inventory includes switchfan, switchpwrbtn and switchbattery.
external_oled.recovery: The OLED author used a long power-button press after the hang. The Lite user attributes the different recovery behavior to the platform power drivers.
external_oled.startup_trials: Three of five ordinary transitions hung. In five trials with other shell GPU clients delayed for ten seconds, all five remained up thirty seconds after those clients resumed.
external_oled.trace_tail: In two early hangs DWM presented four frames, Explorer created its own device, and both clients submitted work. KMD recorded successful preemption requests through the trace tail. No recovery request or reset was captured.
external_oled.longer_session: A separate KMD 0.1.0.203 session hung after about ten minutes of browser and Explorer use.

discriminating_measurements: Confirm the DWM rendering backend before the workload. Compare the same archive workload on Basic Display and the GPU desktop under the same power and Wi-Fi conditions.
Correlate per-client submission, hardware progress, fence retirement, preemption completion and recovery with the first missing progress. Record reset source separately.
graphics_stack_comparison_20261118.root_cause: Unknown. The traces justify prioritizing the shared graphics path, particularly overlapping work from separate GPU clients.

windowed_d3d11_startup_20261118.observation: The first x64 DXVK windowed teapot control loaded application-local DXGI and D3D11. D3D11 hardware device creation returned E_FAIL (0x80004005). No adapter identity or rendered frame was recorded. Only the baseline trial directory and PID were recorded. The candidate measurement never started.
windowed_d3d11_startup_20261118.scope: This is a separate non-PAL4 startup failure. The observed device creation error does not identify the reset source.

subsequent_loader_control.effect: The calibration initially used an executable path missing from the application driver list. Explicitly registering the two test paths allowed enumeration and restored D3D11 device creation on the accepted baseline.

file_integrity_at_restart_20261118.result: All nine invalid cache payloads in three unexpected-restart sessions were entirely zero-filled. All 53 cache files in two application-exit controls passed BLAKE3 verification. The initiating fault is still unknown.

teapot_and_subsequent_logon_20261118.first_scope: Both executables rendered the same scenes. The candidate printed every timing sample after both window checks. Its normal-exit marker was absent after the reset. Write loss prevents assigning the reset to a specific destructor.

following_boot.source: The untriggered test jobs did not restart with Windows. The accepted login controller recorded entry to native activation and did not record its completion. The next boot disabled that controller and used Basic Display.

recovery.input_sources: Windows Kernel-Power event 105 (AcOnline) and the SwitchBattery charge controller status. On this build the charger reports external power when REG08 VBUS_STAT is 1 or 2 and the power-good bit is set.

retry.controller_invocation: The accepted activation controller was invoked once with -Retry. PowerShell line breakpoints recorded its milestones to a write-through journal. No GPU program was launched during the retry.

recovery.interpretation: The later logged-in desktop activation and its 30-second dwell completed on external power, on the same Windows boot that previously held the native GPU at Code 43. Both battery and externally powered resets have been observed in different workloads. These trials do not isolate a power component or identify the cause.

single_pair_timing.scope: These are single 96-iteration runs in the recorded order. The draw and Present times end when the API returns. The candidate had slower mean and P95 in this pair, and its normal exit could not be verified. The candidate was set aside. The accepted WSI source remained in use.

accepted_driver_teardown_control.measurement: RAII markers recorded completion of the normal COM release order, window destruction and return from main. Each transition flushed the application journal to disk. Parent observation confirmed process exit. The time between final window verification and frame report includes writing 96 timing lines.

nvdec_default_device_creation_20261118.status: The owner accepted ded6fa4a for development after a full six-frame default decode. The later unplanned restart is tracked in objective 4, after the objective 5 module reviews.

candidate.capture: In the earlier gate-only comparison the on-device journal recorded successful D3D11VA device creation. Frame and process-exit evidence was incomplete before the separately reported manual restart.

nvdec_default_device_creation_20261118.earlier_candidate_attempts: Three earlier candidate trials were followed by distinct Windows boots with Event 41 and bugcheck zero. One launcher contained a verified pre-FFmpeg PowerShell error. No new watchdog dump identified their cause.

prior_pal4_windows_queue.event: tgd3d event 22, DWM process, stage 3, HRESULT S_OK. Each count is an accepted submission callback. Completion and resource retirement require separate evidence.

sync_questions: For each producer and DWM device, establish its negotiated DDI and whether NVK takes the runtime queue.
Check the ingress and completion fence identities, values, GPU waits and ownership of displayed allocations across the two submission paths. Verify completion before resource and context retirement.
nvdec_default_device_creation_20261118.driver_scope: The gate-only comparison used identical frozen device construction. The accepted UMD adds the checked completion and retirement patch to that source. The KMD and desktop ICD hashes were verified on the accepted boot.

wifi_startup_followup_20261118.status: Deferred by the operator for later investigation.
wifi_startup_followup_20261118.operator_observation: The operator manually restarted the Switch. On that boot the Wi-Fi driver did not come up.
wifi_startup_followup_20261118.effect: Management connectivity returned and the earlier journal was retrieved. The startup issue remains in the platform-driver audit; its manual restart remains excluded from the spontaneous reset count.
wifi_startup_followup_20261118.attribution: Wi-Fi startup is tracked independently. The manual restart is excluded from the count of spontaneous resets. The earlier three distinct boot transitions and their system records are retained separately.
wifi_startup_followup_20261118.when_resumed: Read the Wi-Fi device problem code, driver identity and Kernel-PnP/WLAN startup events for the affected boot before associating the issue with any graphics workload.

native_sequential_first_present_20261120.scope: Physical Switch Lite, external power and Code 0. Ordinary window, two 640-by-360 BGRA buffers, six predecoded 720p NV12 input frames. No video decode submitted.

native_sequential_first_present_20261120.limits: The hardware client validated its requested sequential swap effect. Truncated captures can stop before the first DXGI event or the kernel redirection copy; a successful API return or scanout on an interrupted run cannot be inferred. The desktop capture corroborates logical desktop contents. The behavior of other workloads and the circuit initiating the reset are still unresolved.

native_shared_copy_without_present.scope: Two public D3D11 devices in one process, same adapter. The writer copies to a shared BGRA texture and waits for its event; the reader maps and compares every pixel byte. This does not exercise the Windows redirecting blit DDI.

matching_windows_presentation_runtime.scope: The instructions in the matching native ARM64 runtime contain these direct calls. The interrupted native traces did not preserve a receipt showing which of these operations ran.

native_sequential_gdi_redirection_202611.status: Reproduced on the accepted driver. The underlying cause remains open.
native_sequential_gdi_redirection_202611.scope: One ordinary 640x360 ARM64 D3D11 client, two-buffer windowed sequential swap chain, the same six prerecorded input frames, native desktop compositor and AC power. The drawing device is WARP in the control and GM20B in the native test.

shared_surface_status.meaning: Windows selected a GDI blit for the window redirection surface. The status alone does not distinguish another adapter from system memory. Both drawing devices received it.

native.last_driver_receipt: Both flush(dev, false) and flush(dev, true) returned S_OK. Execution reached the indirect call instruction for pfnPresentCb. The observer did not retain a return from that call.

native_sequential_gdi_redirection_202611.scope_of_evidence: Each named checkpoint was written through from the signed client observer before that thread resumed. Stops affect timing. A missing receipt cannot identify the stalled instruction. Event 41 with bugcheck zero identifies an unclean restart and supplies no stop code. A shared-surface status alone cannot establish which component caused it.

native_gdi_vs_dxgi_after_identical_readb.scope: Both arms use the native drawing adapter, compositor, window, swap chain and six prerecorded source frames. Both copy the GPU-rendered BGRA image to staging, read it back, verify 35 reference pixels per frame, pack all rows, and unmap before window output. The GDI arm calls SetDIBitsToDevice and GdiFlush. The other arm calls DXGI Present(1,0).

native_sequential_pitched_backbuffer_202.status: The trial produced the intended new back buffers. The native first-Present restart still occurred in all three runs. The accepted package was restored.
native_sequential_pitched_backbuffer_202.scope: ARM64 system D3D11 on GM20B, 640x360, two-buffer DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_SEQUENTIAL, external power. Each fresh trial boot first ran the same nonpresenting native render/readback control, then the unchanged signed application with a WARP control followed by native drawing.
native_sequential_pitched_backbuffer_202.trial_change: The windowed BGRA RENDER_TARGET|PRESENT pair uses a pitch-linear, resource-associated allocation. Each no-Present control verified the loaded native leaf, both successful linear binds and six complete peer-device pixel readbacks. The actual presenting process also recorded the two linear allocations.
native_sequential_pitched_backbuffer_202.interpretation: For this client and input, correct pitched storage, Windows resource association and verified readback are insufficient to make the first native sequential Present complete. These measurements leave the initiating reset cause open.

native_sequential_windows_kmt_dispatch_2.status: Unexpected restart on the accepted GM20B stack. The Windows user-mode presentation call boundary is now observed.

versioned_callback.result: This observed Windows compatibility wrapper clears both sync-interval override fields before forwarding to the common callback. The intermediate wrapper that can preserve only the validity flag was not selected by this native test.

native_sequential_windows_kmt_dispatch_2.scope: The last native checkpoint is the user-mode instruction dispatching a D3DKMT_PRESENT. The incomplete kernel trace ends before that instruction. It cannot identify the receiving KMD operation or the initiating reset cause.

window_present_packet_adapter_and_restar.workload: Six prerecorded frames per process, public ARM64 D3D11 FL11_0, 640 by 360, two buffers, Present(1,0). Each run opens WARP SEQUENTIAL first and native GM20B FLIP_SEQUENTIAL second. Both use the same executable and draw input.
window_present_packet_adapter_and_restar.power_control: All launched cases required external power, the accepted native driver and the same power policy. Clock readings are samples before the process, not fixed clocks or measurements at reset.

packet_ownership.join: DxgKrnl packet 178 hContext matches the live Context start/rundown. Its hDevice matches the live Device start/rundown. Its pDxgAdapter matches DpiReportAdapter 110 with the DXGI-reported drawing LUID. Queue completion 180 matches context, packet address, packet type and submit sequence.

warp_redirection.per_frame: Two source surfaces alternate. Windows resolves a single destination. Each full-window copy joins its DMA buffer to queue admission and a matched DMA start and stop.

packet_ownership.history_correlation: Within one process launch, follow the same token from present-history start (215) through info (172) to stop (173) in the actual DWM process. End the search at the next use of that token by any process. The hAdapter field varies between these records on this system. A token stop records DWM consumption of the history entry.
packet_ownership.scope: On the native desktop the WARP copy packet ran on Microsoft Basic Render Driver. That control validates the application and display result. The interrupted native FLIP reports partial progress for its retained frames. Earlier native SEQUENTIAL first-Present restarts remain a separate observation. Presentation completion and final panel latch are different observations.

window_present_packet_adapter_and_restar.restart_observations: The first and third native processes both returned S_OK twice from public Present. Their final write-through marker announces the third chroma UpdateSubresource call. The second native process returned six times, passed desktop sampling and exited. Neither the marker nor its timing identifies a faulting instruction. The third collection spans two recorded Windows starts. The controller has no boot trigger and starts one native client per run.

earlier_preloaded_copy_cross_check.observed: A different native FLIP fixture preloaded all six plane pairs, waited for their GPU completion and used CopyResource for the planes at draw time. Its third frame reached BindPipeline after the two plane copies. It also experienced an unclean restart. Per-frame CPU chroma upload was absent in this earlier case. A shared initiating cause remains unconfirmed.

gm20b_second_flip_idle_and_actual_runtim.scope: Accepted native stack, AC power, normal ARM64 public D3D11 FL11_0, two 640 by 360 BGRA buffers, six prerecorded frames, WARP warm-up and native FLIP_SEQUENTIAL. The same signed test writes two markers after the second native Present returns S_OK. The only test setting is whether the rendering thread sleeps for 2000 milliseconds between the markers. The zero-delay arm also writes both markers.
gm20b_second_flip_idle_and_actual_runtim.conclusion: All three timed waits completed while Windows continued issuing VSync records and the fixture made no new Present or NVK render submission. One timed run restarted after the third Present returned. All three zero-delay runs and the other two timed runs displayed six frames, verified 15 desktop pixels and exited normally. Five native launches shared the same post-recovery boot. This interval does not prevent all restarts.

runtime_queue.receipt: In the matched UMD source, transport event 22 operation 3 surrounds pfnSubmitCommandCb. A matching entry and S_OK return in the same thread records actual Windows callback use. Kernel completion is a separate observation.
runtime_queue.observation: The native render path used the Windows-supplied submit callback in both presentation modes, including first-Present reboot cases. An independent-queue fallback is not a prerequisite for those incidents. The synchronization and later display handoff still require investigation.

native_linear_texture_sampling_shared_fe.hardware: Native GM20B on the same Windows boot, AC, GPU Code 0, two independently created ARM64 hardware D3D11 FL11_0 devices. Each process checked its actual adapter LUID and its loaded native tgd3d leaf.
native_linear_texture_sampling_shared_fe.surface: One 640 by 360 BGRA8 render-target and shader-resource texture shared with IDXGIResource::GetSharedHandle and ID3D11Device::OpenSharedResource. After a full patterned GPU write, subsequent phases include four partial scissored updates. The reader samples the persistent SRV in a pixel shader into a private image. Readback checks every pixel including the areas outside the updated rectangle.

event_query_controls.previous_contents: The second device opened the shared texture after the first writer had finished its first full image. The roles alternate each subsequent phase in the dual-device group. An event query and S_OK device status precede each transfer.

public_shared_fences.comparison: Both modes used two devices and opened an initially painted texture. A wrote phases 0 to 2 and B wrote phases 3 to 5. The first measured full write repeats the initial color pattern. Each phase copied the sampled result to a separate readback resource. Readback validation began only after all six snapshots were enqueued.

gpu_fence_handoff.api: ID3D11Device5::CreateFence and OpenSharedFence, ID3D11Fence::CreateSharedHandle, ID3D11DeviceContext4::Signal and Wait.
gpu_fence_handoff.scope: The measured GPU mode queues work without a per-frame CPU wait. It waits on one event after all six phases are submitted. Pre-call CPU samples describe the value before each Wait call; GPU execution can advance after that sample.

native_linear_texture_sampling_shared_fe.scope: Offscreen sampling exercises shared linear-image ownership, both synchronization directions and partial-update preservation on this workload. Actual window presentation, DWM consumption of a swapchain buffer and panel scanout require separate evidence.

native_first_present_miniport_receipts_2.hardware: Windows ARM64 on GM20B, external AC. Windowed public D3D11 FL11_0, DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_SEQUENTIAL, two 640x360 BGRA buffers and the same six reference frames.
native_first_present_miniport_receipts_2.event_format: Provider c27c1f9b-62e8-4e21-b29b-6bb2d585c6d0, event 5 version 1, keyword 2, 44 bytes. Operation 1 is DxgkDdiPresent entry/return, operation 2 is entry/internal admission of a present-flagged virtual submit, and operation 3 is a successful private adapter query.

Both processes set the runtime-queue option. Windows chooses how to implement BitBlt.

aborted_package_selection.reason: The initial inactive registration referred to the previous runtime directory. The existing boot policy rejected it before issuing a native candidate permit.

first_present_allocation_and_paging.scope: ETW from the drawing PID in each signed public D3D11 test. Count a resource only when one thread entered and returned the same resource operation with a 640x360 render-target/present bind. A successful wait stage may be the fast path. Receipt order within recorded resource creation does not establish GPU ownership at Present.

disposition: Nine unclean reference starts are distinct. The observation kernel trial adds one unclean start before a planned rollback.
Both the live stream and the ETL now contribute miniport entry/return records. Preserve original order within each source for equal timestamps and leave conflicting brackets unknown.
The complete public rectangle-copy control has no matching kernel geometry record. These data do not identify the engine Windows used for that copy.
A truncated ETW cannot exclude a late miniport entry. Each qualified kernel trial includes receipt timestamps relative to the application journal checkpoint when available.

interpretation: Both public native devices completed six render-only frames. The modern empty first Present returned DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED; the same Windows boot and DWM process survived through evidence collection.
The retained kernel events were successful preemption reports. Windows TDR, entry to the earliest reset DDI, and the underlying reason for device removal remain unresolved.
The later UMD error in Device::completed follows the application return. That source site covers a failed semaphore query or an all-ones fence value.
The older legacy empty-window reboots used different driver components. This trial provides a same-boot comparison of the two native render-only paths and a modern first-Present result.

independent_review.source_observation: The WSL guest queries or caches host execution state and can mark a device as erroneous through VMBus. This gives a device-scoped alternative to adapter recovery.
independent_review.qualification: The earliest native reset callback has no entry event. Successful preemption records confirm collection, while a negative reset-event search alone cannot rule out an earlier reset path.
independent_review.next_discriminating_measurement: Read ID3D11Device::GetDeviceRemovedReason before and immediately after the same Present(1,0), before releasing the device. A sync-interval or swap-effect comparison requires a separate case.

conditions.device_reason_query: The original drawing device is sampled before the public call and immediately after it returns, before resource or device destruction.
conditions.interrupted_journal_limit: The same thread writes the durable RETURN marker after reading the post-call device reason. If neither survives, the exact last instruction is unknown.

native_device_removal_reason_and_swap_ef.prior_activity: The first legacy SEQUENTIAL case followed the same-boot matrix. The next two cases were each the first test workload on a freshly admitted candidate boot.
findings: Both modern swap effects changed the device reason from S_OK to DXGI_ERROR_DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR across the first empty Present, with the desktop and boot surviving.
On the same candidate and boot, legacy FLIP_SEQUENTIAL crossed the first Present and then completed six visible reference frames. DirectX kernel present-history model 2 was recorded for each frame.
Missing reset packets on an interrupted trace cannot locate a native TDR. The public removal reason alone does not identify the first failing driver callback.

legacy_durable_umd_callback_control.scope: Qualification of a write-through user-mode receipt on the healthy legacy FLIP_SEQUENTIAL control and readback after a controlled reboot.

public_control.write_mode: FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH and FlushFileBuffers requested after each complete identity-bound record.

historical_kernel_control.source: Previous signed diagnostic KMD and the existing write-through real-time ETW collector.
historical_kernel_control.limit: Persisted entries prove that the kernel receipt channel can survive an actual restart. The recovered Present entries attributed to DWM do not identify the failing drawing process. Event delivery can lag the driver.

observations: The unchanged public application reached the legacy UMD entry and the real Windows callback returned in the positive case.
The record immediately before calling Windows identifies the caller boundary. A callback return or independently attributable downstream record is needed to prove execution inside Windows.
This user-mode recorder covers the DXGI 1.2 normal Present slot. Missing records alone cannot exclude a different DXGI DDI such as Blt or Blt1, or buffered kernel events.
The original three interruptions retain no graphics-driver record after the application call. Their last internal boundary remains unknown.

The older KMD observation package has a different kernel hash. Its write-through ETW consumer retained kernel Present records on DWM threads across actual restarts. This does not establish an application KMD entry in the original three cases.

legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.scope: Normal single-frame native legacy FLIP_SEQUENTIAL on external power. Compare an empty back buffer with a visible clear, then repeat the clear using the ordinary UMD entry without its optional file journal.
legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.control_identity: The preceding healthy UMD journal control on the accepted KMD used the same signed application and ARM64 UMD. The current collector added the installed DxgKrnl Base and Resource device/context events in its existing session.
legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.miniport_path: Each capture received successful adapter queries from the drawing process. The recorded miniport Present entry/return pairs came from DWM threads, with Flip | FlipWithNoWait and zero DMA bytes. The sampled and full miniport logs agree. The v1 miniport record identifies its executing thread and lacks the context field needed for independent object attribution.

legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.synchronization_scope: Both clear cases retired the application GPU write before public Present. Their signal/wait pairs used distinct fences and contexts. The outgoing signal and wait retired. The incoming signal and wait retirements and a subsequent application reuse of the old surface remain unverified in these single-frame captures.
legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.ordinary_control: The ordinary clear matched five desktop samples, retired its application-owned Present packet and reached DWM without any KMD Present recorded during the public call. DWM KMD calls elsewhere in the capture cannot identify the application's miniport entry.
legacy_first_present_kernel_ownership_co.original_incident: Neither retained stream in the original three legacy SEQUENTIAL restarts contains a driver event after the public call. The last internal call and the cause of those restarts remain open. The current observations qualify the healthy flip path.

software_sequential_control_from_archive.display_note: The software sequential control documents the OS copy model. It does not exercise the native GM20B user-mode or miniport implementation for the drawing device.

windows_event_order.scope: This order is relative to the selected events. Windows may execute additional operations. The native flip and software copy controls have different drawing backends.

public_idle_status_on_accepted_profile.scope: Two fresh native GM20B devices tested status after their respective windows left the minimized state. Both use the system D3D11 FL11_0 entry, 640x360 B8G8R8A8_UNORM, two buffers, and the same selected ARM64 driver. The only Present call in the signed client always sets DXGI_PRESENT_TEST.
public_idle_status_on_accepted_profile.interpretation: Windows accepted a visibility/status query on the original sequential model on the daily driver. Testing status alone does not exercise a real presentation, the DWM redirection copy or panel scanout. The original first-frame failure remains open.

wddm20_first_present_driver_dispatch_202.purpose: Find the earliest positively observed driver rejection on the process-local WDDM 2.0 path.
wddm20_first_present_driver_dispatch_202.finding: Present1 receives Reserved=1. The current tgd3d guard returns E_INVALIDARG before its common Present implementation. Both measured windows reported DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED and an immediate DXGI_ERROR_DRIVER_INTERNAL_ERROR device reason.
wddm20_first_present_driver_dispatch_202.contract: Microsoft documents Reserved as a field that should be zero. Both actual calls on this Windows build supplied one. The input was observed, not synthesized.
wddm20_first_present_driver_dispatch_202.scope: The first rejection is established for WDDM 2.0. The initiating cause of the separate legacy SEQUENTIAL system restarts remains open.

native_dxgi_colour_copy_and_shared_desti.scope: Normal legacy ARM64 DXGI Blt and Blt1 on GM20B, including an independent CPU pixel reference, the selected native driver, and a public flip window.
native_dxgi_colour_copy_and_shared_desti.change: An unscaled same-format or compatible sRGB-to-UNORM blit transfers the stored bytes. Filtered encoded data passes through an unsigned-normalized image. A transfer-only linear destination receives one final region copy. A matching explicit-pitch NVK color target retains the private tiled-shadow blit. Scratch storage follows submission retirement.

host_controls.scaling: Checks optimal scratch allocation failure, interior copy bounds, border preservation and retirement after completion.

physical_format_query.qualification: The paired NVK ICD provides an explicit-pitch layout with a tiled color shadow. Public linear masks alone do not establish that a real redirected surface lacks blit destination support.

native_dxgi_colour_copy_and_shared_desti.pixel_criterion: Each case reads a 37 by 29 image. Exact RGBA is required outside a scaled region and for unscaled copies. Filtered interior channels allow a one-unit rounding error.

first_capture.collector_status: The program redirected stdout and stderr into its evidence directory. The controller initially read the empty pipes. The subsequent case archived both files and the journal before cleanup.

original_sequential_backbuffers.interpretation: Each original run read back the requested format and model before its empty first Present. The sRGB source needed for the measured colour conversion error was absent from the application back buffer. The exact internal redirection resource and its DDI were not captured at the crash boundary.
